text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.

Eighty-two state firms will receive 250 million zlotys from the budget to cover debts owed to the state social security office (ZUS). The largest firm to receive such subsidies is the Gliwicka Spolka Weglowa coal firm.
Bank Wschodnio-Europejski bought more than 50 percent of the Passa SA brokerage, becoming the leader of a financial group including the STU insurer and Wschodnio-Europejski's leasing unit.
The Polish unit of Dutch Rabobank, Rabo-BRP Polska SA, will receive a special loan this year allowing it to grant higher credits. The bank will also conduct a capital raise next year.
Central Bank President Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz said the bank might raise interest rates to avoid a banking crisis after the recent credit boom.
President Aleksander Kwasniewski denied rumours that he was not sober at times during his recent visit to the United States.

By the year 2000 all banks belonging to the state treasury should be sold, including shares in Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy (BPH) and Bank Gdanski. The treasury's majority share in Polish Development Bank (PBR) could take part in Poland's bank consolidation process.
